u_\ell$ form factors to experimental data. Our results indicate that the $B	o D\ell
u_\ell$ form factors are consistent with the findings from other theoretical approaches.

We demonstrate that non-invertible symmetries in 4d $\mathcal{N}=2$ superconformal field theories (SCFTs) can be realized as branes within the corresponding 5d superconformal field theories (SCFTs). This approach allows us to construct non-invertible symmetries in 4d $\mathcal{N}=2$ SCFTs by utilizing the 5d superconformal field theories (SCFTs) that are related to them.

We introduce a novel class of graphs, termed symmetric graphs, which are defined by the property that their automorphism group acts transitively on the set of all $k$-tuples of vertices for every $k \geq 1$. We demonstrate that the choiceless polynomial time (CPT) logic is capable of distinguishing these symmetric graphs from all other graphs. Furthermore, we establish that symmetric graphs are precisely those that can be recognized by symmetric circuits. Finally, we prove that the Cai-F\"urer-Immerman graphs are symmetric.

We report on the insulator-to-metal transition observed in the pyrochlore iridate series (Eu1-xBix)2Ir2O7, as investigated via hard X-ray photoemission spectroscopy. Our findings indicate that the transition is driven by the progressive filling of the Ir 5d conduction band, which results from the substitution of Eu3+ with Bi3+.

This paper introduces a novel concept, the core of a set-valued mapping, and establishes existence criteria for Lipschitz selections of low-dimensional set-valued mappings. Furthermore, it presents an efficient algorithm for computing the core of a set-valued mapping.

This paper examines the concept of nontransitive probabilities, which are defined as cyclically ordered probability distributions. We establish that the set of all such distributions forms a convex polytope and provide a complete characterization of its vertices. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the vertices of this polytope correspond to a specific class of cyclically ordered distributions.

This paper introduces a novel approach to compile-time specialization of run-time configuration space, which is a technique for optimizing the performance of software systems. The proposed method is evaluated through an exploratory study that examines its impact on the performance of a range of software systems. The results of the study demonstrate that the proposed method is effective in improving the performance of software systems.

We introduce a novel method for detecting sub-GeV dark matter by utilizing electrons produced during nuclear scattering events. This approach is applicable to both direct detection experiments and collider searches. We demonstrate that this technique can achieve sensitivity to dark matter-nucleon cross sections as low as $10^{-45} \text{ cm}^2$ for dark matter masses between 100 MeV and 1 GeV.

This study examines the dynamics of a two-level atom interacting with a single-mode field within the anti-Jaynes-Cummings framework. We analyze the system's Rabi oscillations, entanglement evolution, and teleportation fidelity. Our findings indicate that the atom-field interaction induces Rabi oscillations, while the atom's entanglement with the field exhibits periodic behavior. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the atom's ability to teleport quantum information is periodic, with the fidelity of this process varying periodically over time.

This study introduces a new method for estimating inter-beat intervals (IBI) using the Tiramisu model, which is a deep learning architecture designed to process time-series data. The proposed approach is evaluated against the widely used RNN-LSTM model, demonstrating that Tiramisu achieves superior performance with lower error rates.

We examine the work fluctuations of an active Ornstein-Uhlenbeck particle (AOUP) moving in a one-dimensional potential. By analyzing the large deviation function of work, we demonstrate that the fluctuation theorem holds for this system. Furthermore, we derive the corresponding fluctuation relation for the entropy production.

This paper introduces HUMBI, a comprehensive dataset designed to facilitate research into human body expression. It features 1,000 individuals performing 100 distinct poses, captured from 12 synchronized cameras. The dataset includes 3D body scans, 2D images, and corresponding annotations for both 2D and 3D keypoints. Additionally, we present a benchmark challenge focused on 3D body pose estimation, with results from the initial challenge available online.

We introduce a novel method for cross-lingual transfer learning that utilizes neural task representations to facilitate model-agnostic knowledge transfer. This approach is designed to be compatible with any pre-trained model, regardless of its architecture. We demonstrate the efficacy of this method through experiments on the cross-lingual sentiment analysis task, showing that it successfully transfers knowledge from English to French.

This study introduces BasicVSR++, an advanced video super-resolution framework that builds upon the original BasicVSR. The proposed method incorporates two key enhancements: a novel propagation module that leverages temporal information to boost feature extraction, and a refined alignment module that utilizes a multi-scale approach to improve the accuracy of frame registration. Experimental results demonstrate that BasicVSR++ achieves superior performance compared to existing state-of-the-art techniques.

This study introduces a novel multi-task reinforcement learning framework that employs modular networks to mitigate catastrophic interference. By utilizing a modular architecture, the system can learn multiple tasks simultaneously while maintaining the ability to perform individual tasks independently. The proposed approach is evaluated on a suite of multi-task environments, demonstrating that it outperforms existing methods in both sample efficiency and final performance.

We examine a finite-time heat engine operating under constrained control, where the engine's power output is limited by a specific constraint. By applying the Pontryagin maximum principle, we derive the optimal control strategy for this scenario. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the optimal control is unique and that the engine's efficiency remains constant throughout the process.

This study examines the spatiotemporal effects of hurricanes and storm surges on power systems, utilizing a case study of Hurricane Sandy. The analysis focuses on the storm surge's impact on the power grid, specifically investigating the relationship between surge height and the duration of power outages. The findings indicate that the surge's influence on power systems is primarily driven by the height of the surge rather than its speed.
This paper establishes a three-balls theorem for the eigenfunctions of the Dirac operator within the framework of Clifford analysis.

We introduce a novel class of heterochaotic baker maps, which are constructed by combining the standard baker map with a specific type of skew product. These maps exhibit a unique property: they possess a unique measure of maximal entropy that is absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure. This result is significant because it demonstrates that the entropy approachability theorem, which holds for all known examples of heterochaotic systems, does not apply universally.

We examine the phenomenology of extended scalar sectors, specifically those featuring a singlet, doublet, and triplet, at future colliders. We analyze the production of these scalars and their subsequent decays, focusing on the distinctive signatures that arise from the triplet's charged components.

This study introduces a novel autoregressive model for generating raw audio waveforms, termed Quasi-Periodic WaveNet. The architecture employs a pitch-dependent dilated convolution neural network to capture the periodic characteristics of sound. The model's efficacy is demonstrated through its ability to synthesize diverse audio types, including speech, music, and environmental sounds.

Collaborative filtering (CF) is a widely adopted technique for addressing the challenge of information overload. However, it faces significant hurdles, including data sparsity, user subjectivity, and the locality of preferences. This paper introduces a novel user-specific bicluster-based CF approach designed to tackle these issues. The proposed method constructs a user-specific bicluster for each individual, which is then utilized to generate personalized recommendations. Experimental results demonstrate that this approach outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency.

This study investigates the influence of solar magnetic activity on disk-integrated spectra obtained by the HARPS-N instrument. We analyze a dataset of 1,000 spectra collected over a 10-year period, utilizing the Ca II H&K line indices to track activity levels. Our findings indicate that activity-induced spectral variations are most pronounced in the Ca II H&K lines and the Mg I b triplet, with the latter showing a 10% change in equivalent width. Conversely, the Fe I lines exhibit minimal sensitivity to activity, with variations limited to 0.01% in equivalent width. Furthermore, we introduce a novel activity indicator based on the Mg I b triplet, which demonstrates a strong correlation with the Ca II H&K index.

We introduce a method to differentiate the Majorana peak from other peaks in tunneling spectroscopy by utilizing resistive electrodes. This approach relies on the fact that the Majorana peak remains unaffected by Ohmic dissipation, whereas other peaks are suppressed. We demonstrate that this technique is applicable to both the topological superconductor and the topological insulator.

We demonstrate that shadows, as defined by Street, are equivalent to bicategorical traces. This result is established by proving that shadows are precisely the bicategorical traces of the identity 1-morphism.

This study introduces a novel framework for learning global tone mapping (GTM) and its inverse (ITM) by distilling style from image pairs. The proposed method employs a dual-stream architecture: one branch learns GTM while the other learns ITM, with both branches jointly trained to minimize the discrepancy between the generated and target images. The experimental results demonstrate that this approach achieves superior performance compared to existing methods.

This report outlines the methodology and results of the team's submission to the 2022 LOVEU AQTC Challenge at CVPR. The approach leverages a pre-trained ResNet-50 model, which is fine-tuned using a custom dataset of 1,000 images. The team achieved a final ranking of 10th place with a score of 0.800.

This study examines the settling of snow in turbulent air, focusing on the preferential sweeping phenomenon. We analyze the vertical velocity of snow particles, which are modeled as passive tracers, and find that their vertical velocity distribution is significantly narrower than that of the surrounding air. This observation indicates that snow particles are swept by the air flow in a preferential manner.

This paper introduces a novel framework for autonomous robot navigation that integrates deep active inference with a deep neural network. The proposed approach utilizes a deep neural network to approximate the generative model, which is then employed to infer the robot's state and select actions. The framework is evaluated through a simulation of a robot navigating a maze, demonstrating its ability to learn a generative model and successfully navigate the environment.

This study introduces a novel Bicephalous Convolutional Autoencoder (BCAE) designed to compress 3D sparse Time Projection Chamber (TPC) data. The proposed architecture employs a dual-branch encoder to extract features from both the sparse and dense representations of the input data, while a single decoder reconstructs the original input. The model is trained using a hybrid loss function that combines reconstruction error with a regularization term to enforce sparsity. Experimental results demonstrate that the BCAE achieves superior compression performance compared to existing methods.

This study examines the statistical properties of galaxy clusters within the Finzi gravity model, which incorporates a repulsive force alongside the standard attractive gravitational interaction. We demonstrate that the model's predictions align with observational data regarding the distribution of galaxy clusters.

This paper investigates the saturation of convex geometric hypergraphs, specifically examining the saturation number of a convex geometric hypergraph $H$ with $n$ vertices, denoted as $\text{sat}(H, n)$. We establish that for any convex geometric hypergraph $H$ with $n$ vertices, the saturation number is bounded by $O(n^2)$. Furthermore, we demonstrate that for any convex geometric hypergraph $H$ with $n$ vertices, the saturation number is bounded by $O(n^2)$.

This study examines the inclusive $\alpha$-particle production in the $^{6}$Li+$^{51}$V system at a beam energy of 100 MeV/nucleon. The experimental data were analyzed using the coupled reaction channels (CRC) model, which incorporates the $\alpha$-particle as a cluster within the $^{6}$Li projectile. The findings indicate that the CRC model successfully reproduces the observed angular distributions of $\alpha$-particles.

The robot's design is inspired by the Pacific Lamprey, a fish that climbs trees to reach spawning grounds. The Pacific Lamprey robot features a flexible body and a specialized head equipped with a suction cup, enabling it to climb by mimicking the fish's natural movement. The robot's body is composed of a series of soft, flexible segments that can bend and twist to navigate obstacles. This study introduces a novel mathematical framework for modeling the immune response to colon cancer, utilizing a Fokker-Planck equation to describe the evolution of the immune cell population. We analyze the system's stability and demonstrate that the immune response can be driven to extinction by a specific type of cancer cell. Furthermore, we derive an optimal control strategy to maximize the immune response, which is shown to be effective in eliminating the cancer.

This study introduces a novel Age of Information (AoI)-driven scheduling framework for wireless device-to-device (D2D) networks, designed to minimize the average AoI across all users. The proposed method employs a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) algorithm to determine optimal scheduling decisions. Simulation results demonstrate that the suggested approach outperforms existing schemes in terms of average AoI.
This study presents an analytical proof of helicity conservation for the compressible Euler equations, utilizing a novel approach that relies on the conservation of the energy-momentum tensor.

This study examines the reflection coefficient for the Davey-Stewartson II equation, which is a nonlinear Schrödinger-type model. We establish that the reflection coefficient decays exponentially as $|k| \to \infty$ for any initial data in the $L^2$ space.

We examine the residual eccentricity of compact binaries at the gravitational-wave detection threshold, utilizing post-Newtonian theory to derive accurate estimates. Our analysis indicates that the residual eccentricity is significantly lower than previously assumed, with the most optimistic scenario yielding a value of $e_{\rm res} \approx 10^{-4}$.

We present a theoretical model for a high-brightness, fully coherent X-ray amplifier seeded by a free-electron laser oscillator. This system utilizes a free-electron laser oscillator to generate a coherent seed, which is then amplified by a free-electron laser amplifier. The model demonstrates that the system can achieve a high degree of coherence and brightness, making it a promising candidate for future X-ray applications.

This paper introduces a novel framework for identifying events within dynamic graphs, where an event is defined as a specific subgraph that emerges and subsequently vanishes over time. We propose a new algorithm capable of detecting these events in real-time, and we demonstrate its effectiveness through experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets.

The rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has introduced significant challenges, particularly regarding the "black box" nature of many algorithms. This opacity hinders the ability to understand how decisions are made, thereby limiting trust and adoption. Consequently, Explainable AI (XAI) has emerged as a vital research field aimed at enhancing the interpretability of AI systems. While XAI is frequently discussed from a technical standpoint, this paper proposes a user-centric approach to defining XAI requirements. By examining the specific needs of end-users, the study identifies key requirements for explainability and outlines a methodology for eliciting them.

Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains the second most prevalent malignancy globally, with early detection through colonoscopy being the primary method for identifying precancerous polyps. While current clinical practice relies on visual inspection by pathologists, this approach is prone to subjectivity and inter-observer variability. To address this, we introduce UniToPatho, a novel dataset comprising 1,000 annotated histopathological images of colorectal polyps. This collection includes 100 images each for normal, adenoma, and carcinoma categories, alongside 700 images of adenomas further classified by dysplasia grade. The dataset is designed to facilitate the development of automated systems for polyp classification and dysplasia grading, thereby enhancing diagnostic accuracy and consistency.

This study examines the information leakage inherent in zero-error source coding, a scenario where a source is compressed into a smaller alphabet while guaranteeing that the original message can be perfectly recovered. We establish a graph-theoretic framework to analyze this leakage, demonstrating that it is bounded by the logarithm of the graph's independence number. Furthermore, we derive a lower bound for leakage in terms of the graph's chromatic number.

This study introduces a novel deep generative prior for synthetic aperture radar (SAR) image super-resolution, termed MrSARP. The model employs a hierarchical architecture that integrates a convolutional autoencoder with a conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN) to enhance the resolution of low-quality SAR imagery. The proposed method is evaluated against existing state-of-the-art techniques using both simulated and real-world datasets, demonstrating superior performance in terms of both quantitative metrics and visual quality.

This study introduces a Bayesian optimization framework designed to enhance the performance of the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) by efficiently identifying optimal parameters. We demonstrate that this method surpasses standard random search techniques in both speed and effectiveness. Furthermore, we show that the approach is capable of locating the global optimum for the MaxCut problem on a 10-vertex graph.

This paper presents a method for determining the area of intersection between two ellipses. The approach involves transforming the ellipses into circles, calculating the overlap of these circles, and then applying the inverse transformation to obtain the final result.

This paper introduces a continuous-time q-learning algorithm designed for Markov decision processes (MDPs) with continuous state and action spaces. The method employs a discretized version of the q-function to approximate the optimal q-function, which is then updated using a stochastic gradient descent approach. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that the algorithm converges to the optimal q-function under specific conditions.

We investigate the magnetic excitations and phase diagram of the extended triangular-lattice Hubbard model using a combination of exact diagonalization and dynamical mean-field theory. Our findings reveal that the system exhibits a rich phase diagram featuring a Mott insulator, a ferromagnetic metal, and a paramagnetic metal. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the paramagnetic metal phase is stabilized by order-by-disorder mechanisms.

This study introduces a novel framework for automatically localizing and identifying vertebrae in CT scans. The method employs a two-stage process: first, a spine rectification module aligns the spine to a standard orientation, and second, an anatomically-constrained optimization module identifies each vertebra. The rectification module utilizes a 3D convolutional neural network to generate a 3D heatmap of the spine, which is then refined by a 3D deformable model to produce a rectified spine. The identification module uses a 3D deformable model to locate individual vertebrae, guided by a cost function that incorporates anatomical constraints. The proposed method was evaluated on the MURA dataset, demonstrating superior performance compared to existing methods.

We examine the fluctuation statistics of currents in stochastic thermodynamics, specifically focusing on the gauge invariance of their asymptotic behavior. We demonstrate that the large deviation function governing the current's statistics remains invariant under gauge transformations, provided the transformation is applied consistently to both the system's dynamics and the current's definition. This invariance is established by proving that the large deviation function is determined by the spectrum of a specific non-Hermitian operator, which itself is gauge invariant.

We present a theoretical model for the complete tunneling of acoustic waves between two closely spaced piezoelectric crystals. This phenomenon is achieved by applying a voltage to the crystals, which creates a potential barrier that can be tuned to allow for full wave transmission.

We introduce a reservoir optical framework for exciton-polariton condensates, which accounts for the influence of the reservoir on the condensate's dynamics. This model is derived from a microscopic Hamiltonian and incorporates the reservoir's impact on the condensate's energy and momentum. We demonstrate that the reservoir can induce a shift in the condensate's momentum, which is a key factor in the formation of a reservoir-induced condensate.

We present the first detection of a dust disk around the exoplanet K2-22 b, a sub-Neptune orbiting a K-type star. Utilizing the Large Binocular Telescope, we observed the system in the near-infrared and identified a significant excess in the 1.6 μm band, which is attributed to dust grains with radii of approximately 10 μm. This finding indicates that the planet is actively shedding mass at a rate of roughly 10⁻⁷ M⊕ per year.

This paper establishes a consistency theorem for Milnor fibers of isolated singularities, demonstrating that the Milnor fiber of a generic slice through the critical locus of a function $f$ is homotopy equivalent to the Milnor fiber of the restriction of $f$ to that slice. The proof relies on the flatness of the critical locus, a property derived from the work of Kollár and Saito.

This paper introduces Daany, a novel tool designed to analyze .NET applications by examining their runtime behavior. The system operates by monitoring the execution of a target application and collecting data on its runtime activities. This data is then processed to generate a comprehensive report detailing the application's behavior.

This paper examines the relationship between mathematics and philosophy during the Scientific Revolution, specifically analyzing the works of Galileo and Descartes. It argues that the Scientific Revolution was not merely a shift in scientific methodology but also a significant transformation in the nature of philosophy.

We investigate the non-Gaussian signatures of the Saha ionization epoch within the early universe, focusing on the impact of the transition from a radiation-dominated to a matter-dominated era. By analyzing the primordial power spectrum and bispectrum, we demonstrate that the Saha transition generates a distinctive non-Gaussian feature in the bispectrum, which is absent in the standard radiation-to-matter transition. This specific signature is characterized by a peak in the bispectrum at a wavenumber $k$ corresponding to the horizon scale at the moment of recombination.

This study investigates the merging of magnetic islands in a tokamak plasma by employing a hybrid approach that combines magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) with an adaptively embedded particle-in-cell (PIC) model. The simulation setup features a circular magnetic island within a plasma environment, where the PIC method is utilized to resolve the kinetic behavior of electrons in the island's interior, while the MHD framework governs the surrounding plasma. The results demonstrate that the PIC model accurately captures the kinetic dynamics of electrons within the island, whereas the MHD model effectively describes the global plasma evolution. Furthermore, the study reveals that the merging process is driven by the kinetic effects of electrons in the island's core, which generate a localized current that facilitates the coalescence.

This paper introduces Amanuensis, a system designed to assist programmers by generating code from natural language descriptions. The system operates by first parsing the input into a semantic representation, then utilizing a large language model to produce the corresponding code. The authors evaluated the system's performance on a dataset of 1,000 programming tasks, demonstrating that it achieves a 40% success rate in generating correct solutions.
